# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the comment claims "the SSE consumption below keeps its own pacing" — it doesn't; codex mid-stream stalls still hang forever**

`run()` consumes the body with a raw loop:

```dart
await for (final line
    in response.stream
        .transform(utf8.decoder)
        .transform(const LineSplitter())) { ... }
```

There is no idle watchdog anywhere on this path — the shared `createSseIterator` / `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` (provider_common.dart) is what gives the *other* adapters their `providerStreamIdleTimeout` pacing, and codex bypasses it (`grep -n "sseIdle\|idleWatchdog\|streamIdle" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` → nothing; `test/providers/sse_idle_watchdog_test.dart` doesn't cover codex). `grep -n "timeout(" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` shows only this new send timeout.

Suggestion: route the codex consumption through `createSseIterator(response, cancelToken)` like the other adapters (gives the idle watchdog + the issue-#921 safe abandonment for free), or at minimum correct this comment so the audit table's "streaming adapters … + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact" claim is true for codex.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the read-leg timeout abandons the response body without cancelling/draining it**

On read timeout, `http.Response.fromStream(streamed).timeout(read, …)` leaves the body subscription alive and nobody drains or cancels it:

- The socket can never return to the keep-alive pool (undrained response), and a server that keeps trickling bytes into the abandoned stream buffers them until the socket dies.
- On the **shared** client this poisons a pooled connection: `chatgpt_codex.dart:341` passes the shared keep-alive client into `refreshChatGptCredentials` → `_tokenRequest` → `sendProviderFetch`, and `runProviderStream` never closes it (`ownsClient: false`). This is the same abandonment class issue #921 solved for the SSE path (`_IdleWatchdogSseIterator`'s `onAbandon` + owned error sink).

The docstring's ceiling note covers the *connect* leg (no headers yet — nothing to drain). For the read leg a cheap improvement: race `fromStream` against a timer and on timeout `unawaited(streamed.stream.drain<void>().timeout(...))` (or listen-and-cancel), so the connection closes/reuses cleanly.

Related nit: `aiin_auth.dart:415` creates `http.Client()` when `client == null` and never closes it — `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` right next door shows the `ownsClient` + `finally { httpClient.close() }` pattern; adopting it bounds the leak on this path too.

blocks.text:
Good — `google.dart:16` explicitly documents "the `?key=` query-param alternative is not used" (it uses the `x-goog-api-key` header instead). Let me verify the other queryParameters users:
- aiin_auth.dart:154 — the OAuth authorize URL query params (code/challenge — public PKCE params, not secrets; also this is a BROWSER-redirect URL, not a provider stream request that would hit `_sendWatched`).
- chatgpt_oauth.dart:126 — authorize endpoint params (PKCE, public).
- dial.dart:93 — api-version. Not a secret.
- openrouter_oauth.dart:123 — auth endpoint params.

So no provider secret rides the request URL of streaming requests. What about CUSTOM providers (`customProviders` with a baseUrl that itself embeds a key in the query, e.g. `https://host/v1?key=SECRET`)? A user COULD configure a custom baseUrl with a key in it. Then `_sendWatched`'s timeout message would leak it into the transcript/session JSONL. Precedent in-repo: how do other error messages handle URLs? `ProviderHttpError.requestUrl` — stored but the rendered message is `statusCode: body` (URL not rendered except in the auth-expired marker case, which is host-targeted). Also `stripAuthExpiredMarker`... Let me check if anything else renders full request URLs in messages: `redaction` — the redaction pipeline would mask? The transcript redaction masks secrets in tool results/transforms — errorMessage from provider streams: does transformContext redact outgoing, and session persist redacts afterToolCall — but assistant errorMessage? The redaction hooks: "afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext masks the outgoing context, redactPrompt masks user input" — assistant messages are NOT masked by those (no redactAssistant). Hmm — but the session file would contain the assistant error message.

Risk assessment: the built-in catalog providers don't put keys in URLs (verified). A custom provider with an in-URL key is user-configured — the user would already have the key in their config; leaking it into the session transcript is still a (minor) hygiene regression vs the old message that carried no URL. The previous behavior for `_sendWatched` was the anonymous "Future timed out after 3:00" — no URL. So round 2 introduced URL rendering into the timeout message — a NEW (edge-case) secret-leak vector for custom providers whose baseUrl embeds credentials. What's the right call? Compare: `sendProviderFetch` messages use `endpoint` labels (host-only) — deliberately safe. The codex messages use `$_endpoint` — the codex endpoint URL is `${model.baseUrl}/responses` where baseUrl is the ChatGPT backend URL (no secret). For `_sendWatched` (ALL streaming adapters, incl. CUSTOM providers), embedding the full URL is inconsistent with the host-only pattern used elsewhere in the same PR.

I'd class this as IMPORTANT (security hygiene): render the host (or sanitize query) instead of the full URL — e.g. `${request.url.host}` matches the aiin pattern (`aiin auth (${url.host})`), keeping the message useful without reproducing any user-embedded credential. Hmm — but is it really IMPORTANT? "Real maintainability or correctness issue" — a potential credential leak into persisted session files for custom-provider configs. The severity guide: BLOCKING = merge would cause a security issue. This IS a security-ish issue but conditional on a user config choice. The repo's own review history (SEC-01 trust boundary comments) shows they take credential-leak-to-unexpected-places seriously. I'll rank IMPORTANT (not BLOCKING since built-in providers are safe and the key would be the user's own, rendered back into the user's own session file — not exfiltrated anywhere). Reasonable.

3. Codex `_consumeSseLines` correctness — check `unawaited(lines.cancel().then(...))` on clean end: cancel after stream exhausted completes fine. On the idle-timeout exit: moveNext abandoned + cancel pending-moveNext — SDK behavior: `StreamIterator.cancel` while moveNext pending — need to be sure it doesn't throw "Already waiting" or similar. The SDK's StreamIterator.cancel documentation: "Cancels the stream iterator... If the stream iterator is in the middle of a moveNext call (i.e., the future returned by moveNext has not yet completed), the cancel future will wait until..." Actually let me check the Dart SDK source to be certain this is legal and safe.

Actually — `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` (the existing, shipped pattern) does exactly `unawaited(_quietCancel(_inner.cancel()))` where `_inner` is a plain `StreamIterator` whose moveNext may well be pending when the idle timer fires. So cancel-while-pending is the established in-repo pattern — proven in production. The codex code mirrors it. Safe.

One more difference though: the shared iterator OWNS the raw subscription via a StreamController with an error sink swallowing post-abandonment errors (#921). The codex version transforms `response.stream` directly. Cancel propagates: StreamIterator.cancel → cancels the fused subscription → _StreamHandlerTransformer.cancel propagates to raw subscription.cancel → socket detached, no more errors delivered. Between timeout-fire and cancel-completion there's a microtask window where a raw error could arrive at... the pending moveNext's internal listener — which was abandoned via Future.timeout (source errors after timeout are consumed by the timeout machinery). And any error AFTER cancel → not delivered. But what about an error arriving between the timeout throwing and the finally executing? Same microtask — the finally runs synchronously after the throw propagates. And errors delivered to a subscription whose listener chain is mid-cancel → routed to the pending moveNext completer → consumed by timeout's internal listener. OK — safe in practice, matches the guardrails. The late-failure-after-cancel case: subscription cancelled → no delivery. So the #921 crash class is avoided. ✓

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1108
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1108
- **Title**: fix(#1036): bound provider HTTP calls with client-side timeouts
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1036` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +406
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T11:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T12:18:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1036

## What hung, what is bounded now

Audited every provider HTTP call in `lib/src/providers/` (the shared `sharedProviderHttpClient` plus every direct `http.Client` use):

| Path | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `aiin_auth._postOrGet` (OAuth providers list, code exchange, API-key registration) | **no timeout at all** — the issue's hang | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s) |
| `chatgpt_codex._request` (`/responses` send) | **no watchdog** — the only unbounded send in the streaming adapters | `.timeout(effectiveProviderConnectTimeout)` with a message naming the endpoint (same bound as `_sendWatched`) |
| `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` (exchange + refresh) | hard-coded 30s, not configurable | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s, configurable) |
| models lists (`models_for_endpoint`, 4 dialects) | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate fail-fast prefetch budget |
| remote catalog | 10s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| codemie sso (3 calls) / openrouter oauth | 30s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| dial models info | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| copilot device flow + token exchange | `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` | unchanged — already configurable via yaml |
| streaming adapters (anthropic, google, dial, openai, copilot, llm relay) | `sendProviderRequest`/`_sendWatched` + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact (all existing watchdog tests pass) |

On timeout every fixed path fails with a `TimeoutException` whose message names the endpoint class and the leg (connect vs read) — aiin wraps into `AiinAuthException`, ChatGPT OAuth into `ConfigException`, codex surfaces via the errors-as-events `ErrorEvent` (message rendered bare by the new `formatProviderError` `TimeoutException` branch). The agent can retry/degrade; it never hangs.

## Env override precedence (one resolution order, documented)

`FA_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (positive integer seconds) folds into the EXISTING `providerTimeoutsOverride` mechanism at boot (`applyProviderTimeoutEnvOverride` in `cli_config.dart`, called from `bin/fah.dart`) — it sets the new `ProviderTimeoutsOverride.fetchRead` field. Resolution order: **env wins over the `providerTimeouts:` yaml section, both win over the defaults** (a CI runner tightens the bound without editing `~/.fah/config.yaml`; same env-wins pattern as `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Per-field: the yaml section keeps governing `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the env var governs only the non-streaming fetch read bound. Invalid values fail loud with a `ConfigException` naming the env var.

Defaults: read 120s, connect 30s — the connect leg is capped by the read budget, so one knob tightens both.

Scope notes:
- the env override is per-boot: the resilience settings flow re-publishes `providerTimeoutsOverride` from the yaml section on write, which drops an env-set `fetchRead` until restart (documented behavior, not worth extra state).
- no new yaml key (`fetchReadTimeoutMs`) — env-only by design; add a yaml key when file-level control is actually needed.

## Ask-item 3 (watchdog resume poisoning) — follow-up, not implemented

No poisoned-session machinery exists in-repo; marking sessions after a provider-hang death needs death-cause tracking from the external FA-TRACE-STALE-WATCHDOG through session state and a skip rule in `--continue` — not a small clean addition. With items 1+2 the scenario dissolves in practice: the resume can no longer re-enter an unbounded call — the same call now errors within ≤150s and the resumed turn makes visible progress.

## Verification

TDD: red first (hanging `MockClient` on each fixed path), then green:
- new tests: `sendProviderFetch` connect/read legs + defaults + env cap; aiin hanging endpoint; ChatGPT OAuth hanging token endpoint; codex hanging `/responses` send → `ErrorEvent` names endpoint + timeout; env fold (valid/blank/invalid).
- targeted suites all green: provider_common, aiin_auth, chatgpt_oauth, chatgpt_codex, cli_config (198) + codemie_sso, copilot_device_flow, remote_catalog, models_for_endpoint, dial, openrouter_oauth, sse_idle_watchdog, shared_http_client, codex_transport, settings_flow_resilience (155). Streaming-path watchdog tests (sse_idle_watchdog, existing codex/copilot suites) pass untouched.
- `dart analyze` scoped to changed surfaces: no issues.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: bare TimeoutException rendering breaks failover/queue classification for every watchdog timeout**

The new branch in `formatProviderError` renders `TimeoutException` bare (no `"TimeoutException: "` prefix). But the rendered `errorMessage` is the *contract* the model-roles failover chain and the providers-queue runtime classify on:

- `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart` `_transportPatterns` matches `timeout ?exception` / `request (attempt )?timed? ?out` — its own doc comment says watchdog timeouts are "always retryable", and `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart:1295` pins `'TimeoutException after 0:03:00.000000: Future not completed'` as transient (that shape came from `TimeoutException.toString()`, which the new branch no longer renders).
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` `_timeoutPatterns` matches `timeout ?exception` the same way.

Verified empirically against `isTransientTransportError` — all of these now classify **false** (pre-PR they were `true` via the `TimeoutException` word in `toString()`):

| Message (as rendered post-PR) | transient? |
|---|---|
| `Future timed out after 3:00` (`_sendWatched` connect watchdog, all streaming adapters) | ❌ was ✅ |
| `no events from the endpoint for 300s (stream idle timeout)` (SSE idle watchdog, all adapters) | ❌ was ✅ |
| `provider fetch (…): no response headers within 30s (connect watchdog)` | ❌ |
| `provider fetch (…): response did not complete within 120s (read watchdog…)` | ❌ |
| `chatgpt-codex … timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)` | ❌ |

Consequence: a wedged endpoint that times out now produces a **non-retryable** error — the resolver no longer fails over (`fallback_stream`) and the queue runtime no longer records a `QueueDeathKind.timeout` (`providers_queue_runtime.dart`). Per AGENTS.md, watchdogs exist "so a wedged endpoint errors out — and the resolver can fail over"; this PR severs that link for the exact failure class it adds messages for. The PR's targeted suites passed because `fallback_stream_test.dart` pins raw text inputs and never runs `formatProviderError` output end-to-end.

**Fix (pick one, but make it end-to-end tested):**
1. Keep a classifier-compatible keyword in the rendered text (e.g. render `TimeoutException: ${error.message}`), **or**
2. Add a pattern the new shapes match (e.g. `\btimed? ?out\b` / `watchdog`) to `_transportPatterns` and `_timeoutPatterns`, **and**
3. Give `_sendWatched` a named `onTimeout` message like the codex/fetch watchdogs got — its anonymous `Future timed out after …` currently matches nothing even in text form;
4. Extend `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart` + the queue tests to classify the *actual* `formatProviderError(TimeoutException)` output for all five shapes above.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the comment claims "the SSE consumption below keeps its own pacing" — it doesn't; codex mid-stream stalls still hang forever**

`run()` consumes the body with a raw loop:

```dart
await for (final line
    in response.stream
        .transform(utf8.decoder)
        .transform(const LineSplitter())) { ... }
```

There is no idle watchdog anywhere on this path — the shared `createSseIterator` / `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` (provider_common.dart) is what gives the *other* adapters their `providerStreamIdleTimeout` pacing, and codex bypasses it (`grep -n "sseIdle\|idleWatchdog\|streamIdle" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` → nothing; `test/providers/sse_idle_watchdog_test.dart` doesn't cover codex). `grep -n "timeout(" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` shows only this new send timeout.

So after headers arrive (the leg this PR bounds), an endpoint that stalls mid-SSE still hangs the turn indefinitely — `cancelToken.throwIfCancelled()` only helps when a token exists. That is precisely the "resume re-entered the same hang" scenario the PR says "dissolves in practice" once items 1+2 land: for codex it does not.

Suggestion: route the codex consumption through `createSseIterator(response, cancelToken)` like the other adapters (gives the idle watchdog + the issue-#921 safe abandonment for free), or at minimum correct this comment so the audit table's "streaming adapters … + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact" claim is true for codex.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the read-leg timeout abandons the response body without cancelling/draining it**

On read timeout, `http.Response.fromStream(streamed).timeout(read, …)` leaves the body subscription alive and nobody drains or cancels it:

- The socket can never return to the keep-alive pool (undrained response), and a server that keeps trickling bytes into the abandoned stream buffers them until the socket dies.
- On the **shared** client this poisons a pooled connection: `chatgpt_codex.dart:341` passes the shared keep-alive client into `refreshChatGptCredentials` → `_tokenRequest` → `sendProviderFetch`, and `runProviderStream` never closes it (`ownsClient: false`). This is the same abandonment class issue #921 solved for the SSE path (`_IdleWatchdogSseIterator`'s `onAbandon` + owned error sink).

The docstring's ceiling note covers the *connect* leg (no headers yet — nothing to drain). For the read leg a cheap improvement: race `fromStream` against a timer and on timeout `unawaited(streamed.stream.drain<void>().timeout(...))` (or listen-and-cancel), so the connection closes/reuses cleanly.

Related nit: `aiin_auth.dart:415` creates `http.Client()` when `client == null` and never closes it — `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` right next door shows the `ownsClient` + `finally { httpClient.close() }` pattern; adopting it bounds the leak on this path too.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1108
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1108
- **Title**: fix(#1036): bound provider HTTP calls with client-side timeouts
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1036` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +406
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T11:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T12:18:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1036

## What hung, what is bounded now

Audited every provider HTTP call in `lib/src/providers/` (the shared `sharedProviderHttpClient` plus every direct `http.Client` use):

| Path | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `aiin_auth._postOrGet` (OAuth providers list, code exchange, API-key registration) | **no timeout at all** — the issue's hang | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s) |
| `chatgpt_codex._request` (`/responses` send) | **no watchdog** — the only unbounded send in the streaming adapters | `.timeout(effectiveProviderConnectTimeout)` with a message naming the endpoint (same bound as `_sendWatched`) |
| `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` (exchange + refresh) | hard-coded 30s, not configurable | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s, configurable) |
| models lists (`models_for_endpoint`, 4 dialects) | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate fail-fast prefetch budget |
| remote catalog | 10s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| codemie sso (3 calls) / openrouter oauth | 30s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| dial models info | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| copilot device flow + token exchange | `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` | unchanged — already configurable via yaml |
| streaming adapters (anthropic, google, dial, openai, copilot, llm relay) | `sendProviderRequest`/`_sendWatched` + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact (all existing watchdog tests pass) |

On timeout every fixed path fails with a `TimeoutException` whose message names the endpoint class and the leg (connect vs read) — aiin wraps into `AiinAuthException`, ChatGPT OAuth into `ConfigException`, codex surfaces via the errors-as-events `ErrorEvent` (message rendered bare by the new `formatProviderError` `TimeoutException` branch). The agent can retry/degrade; it never hangs.

## Env override precedence (one resolution order, documented)

`FA_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (positive integer seconds) folds into the EXISTING `providerTimeoutsOverride` mechanism at boot (`applyProviderTimeoutEnvOverride` in `cli_config.dart`, called from `bin/fah.dart`) — it sets the new `ProviderTimeoutsOverride.fetchRead` field. Resolution order: **env wins over the `providerTimeouts:` yaml section, both win over the defaults** (a CI runner tightens the bound without editing `~/.fah/config.yaml`; same env-wins pattern as `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Per-field: the yaml section keeps governing `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the env var governs only the non-streaming fetch read bound. Invalid values fail loud with a `ConfigException` naming the env var.

Defaults: read 120s, connect 30s — the connect leg is capped by the read budget, so one knob tightens both.

Scope notes:
- the env override is per-boot: the resilience settings flow re-publishes `providerTimeoutsOverride` from the yaml section on write, which drops an env-set `fetchRead` until restart (documented behavior, not worth extra state).
- no new yaml key (`fetchReadTimeoutMs`) — env-only by design; add a yaml key when file-level control is actually needed.

## Ask-item 3 (watchdog resume poisoning) — follow-up, not implemented

No poisoned-session machinery exists in-repo; marking sessions after a provider-hang death needs death-cause tracking from the external FA-TRACE-STALE-WATCHDOG through session state and a skip rule in `--continue` — not a small clean addition. With items 1+2 the scenario dissolves in practice: the resume can no longer re-enter an unbounded call — the same call now errors within ≤150s and the resumed turn makes visible progress.

## Verification

TDD: red first (hanging `MockClient` on each fixed path), then green:
- new tests: `sendProviderFetch` connect/read legs + defaults + env cap; aiin hanging endpoint; ChatGPT OAuth hanging token endpoint; codex hanging `/responses` send → `ErrorEvent` names endpoint + timeout; env fold (valid/blank/invalid).
- targeted suites all green: provider_common, aiin_auth, chatgpt_oauth, chatgpt_codex, cli_config (198) + codemie_sso, copilot_device_flow, remote_catalog, models_for_endpoint, dial, openrouter_oauth, sse_idle_watchdog, shared_http_client, codex_transport, settings_flow_resilience (155). Streaming-path watchdog tests (sse_idle_watchdog, existing codex/copilot suites) pass untouched.
- `dart analyze` scoped to changed surfaces: no issues.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

Key review areas:

1. **Resource leak in `sendProviderFetch`**: when `Response.fromStream` times out, the underlying `StreamedResponse` is abandoned but its stream subscription is not cancelled. Same on connect timeout — the `client.send(request)` future is abandoned. The docstring acknowledges: "The underlying socket is not force-closed on timeout (same ceiling as the streaming connect watchdog)". For the read leg, when `http.Response.fromStream(streamed)` times out, the streamed response's stream keeps buffering. Actually with package:http, if the response stream is not fully read/closed, the connection remains open. Over time this could leak sockets. The doc acknowledges it. It matches existing patterns presumably (`_sendWatched` similar). Let me check `_sendWatched` in provider_common.dart.

2. **`bin/fah.dart` try/catch** — `applyProviderTimeoutEnvOverride` throws `ConfigException` for invalid values → `_fail`. Good.

3. **In `aiin_auth.dart`**: previously `(client ?? http.Client()).send(request)` — note that when `client == null`, a NEW `http.Client()` was created and... was it closed? Let me check the original code — `final response = await (client ?? http.Client()).send(request);` The fresh client was never closed, but that existed before. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: bare TimeoutException rendering breaks failover/queue classification for every watchdog timeout**

The new branch in `formatProviderError` renders `TimeoutException` bare (no `"TimeoutException: "` prefix). But the rendered `errorMessage` is the *contract* the model-roles failover chain and the providers-queue runtime classify on:

- `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart` `_transportPatterns` matches `timeout ?exception` / `request (attempt )?timed? ?out` — its own doc comment says watchdog timeouts are "always retryable", and `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart:1295` pins `'TimeoutException after 0:03:00.000000: Future not completed'` as transient (that shape came from `TimeoutException.toString()`, which the new branch no longer renders).
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` `_timeoutPatterns` matches `timeout ?exception` the same way.

Verified empirically against `isTransientTransportError` — all of these now classify **false** (pre-PR they were `true` via the `TimeoutException` word in `toString()`):

| Message (as rendered post-PR) | transient? |
|---|---|
| `Future timed out after 3:00` (`_sendWatched` connect watchdog, all streaming adapters) | ❌ was ✅ |
| `no events from the endpoint for 300s (stream idle timeout)` (SSE idle watchdog, all adapters) | ❌ was ✅ |
| `provider fetch (…): no response headers within 30s (connect watchdog)` | ❌ |
| `provider fetch (…): response did not complete within 120s (read watchdog…)` | ❌ |
| `chatgpt-codex … timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)` | ❌ |

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the comment claims "the SSE consumption below keeps its own pacing" — it doesn't; codex mid-stream stalls still hang forever**

`run()` consumes the body with a raw loop:

```dart
await for (final line
    in response.stream
        .transform(utf8.decoder)
        .transform(const LineSplitter())) { ... }
```

There is no idle watchdog anywhere on this path — the shared `createSseIterator` / `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` (provider_common.dart) is what gives the *other* adapters their `providerStreamIdleTimeout` pacing, and codex bypasses it (`grep -n "sseIdle\|idleWatchdog\|streamIdle" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` → nothing; `test/providers/sse_idle_watchdog_test.dart` doesn't cover codex). `grep -n "timeout(" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` shows only this new send timeout.

So after headers arrive (the leg this PR bounds), an endpoint that stalls mid-SSE still hangs the turn indefinitely — `cancelToken.throwIfCancelled()` only helps when a token exists. That is precisely the "resume re-entered the same hang" scenario the PR says "dissolves in practice" once items 1+2 land: for codex it does not.

Suggestion: route the codex consumption through `createSseIterator(response, cancelToken)` like the other adapters (gives the idle watchdog + the issue-#921 safe abandonment for free), or at minimum correct this comment so the audit table's "streaming adapters … + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact" claim is true for codex.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the read-leg timeout abandons the response body without cancelling/draining it**

On read timeout, `http.Response.fromStream(streamed).timeout(read, …)` leaves the body subscription alive and nobody drains or cancels it:

- The socket can never return to the keep-alive pool (undrained response), and a server that keeps trickling bytes into the abandoned stream buffers them until the socket dies.
- On the **shared** client this poisons a pooled connection: `chatgpt_codex.dart:341` passes the shared keep-alive client into `refreshChatGptCredentials` → `_tokenRequest` → `sendProviderFetch`, and `runProviderStream` never closes it (`ownsClient: false`). This is the same abandonment class issue #921 solved for the SSE path (`_IdleWatchdogSseIterator`'s `onAbandon` + owned error sink).

The docstring's ceiling note covers the *connect* leg (no headers yet — nothing to drain). For the read leg a cheap improvement: race `fromStream` against a timer and on timeout `unawaited(streamed.stream.drain<void>().timeout(...))` (or listen-and-cancel), so the connection closes/reuses cleanly.

Related nit: `aiin_auth.dart:415` creates `http.Client()` when `client == null` and never closes it — `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` right next door shows the `ownsClient` + `finally { httpClient.close() }` pattern; adopting it bounds the leak on this path too.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1108
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1108
- **Title**: fix(#1036): bound provider HTTP calls with client-side timeouts
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1036` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +406
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T11:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T12:18:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1036

## What hung, what is bounded now

Audited every provider HTTP call in `lib/src/providers/` (the shared `sharedProviderHttpClient` plus every direct `http.Client` use):

| Path | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `aiin_auth._postOrGet` (OAuth providers list, code exchange, API-key registration) | **no timeout at all** — the issue's hang | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s) |
| `chatgpt_codex._request` (`/responses` send) | **no watchdog** — the only unbounded send in the streaming adapters | `.timeout(effectiveProviderConnectTimeout)` with a message naming the endpoint (same bound as `_sendWatched`) |
| `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` (exchange + refresh) | hard-coded 30s, not configurable | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s, configurable) |
| models lists (`models_for_endpoint`, 4 dialects) | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate fail-fast prefetch budget |
| remote catalog | 10s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| codemie sso (3 calls) / openrouter oauth | 30s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| dial models info | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| copilot device flow + token exchange | `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` | unchanged — already configurable via yaml |
| streaming adapters (anthropic, google, dial, openai, copilot, llm relay) | `sendProviderRequest`/`_sendWatched` + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact (all existing watchdog tests pass) |

On timeout every fixed path fails with a `TimeoutException` whose message names the endpoint class and the leg (connect vs read) — aiin wraps into `AiinAuthException`, ChatGPT OAuth into `ConfigException`, codex surfaces via the errors-as-events `ErrorEvent` (message rendered bare by the new `formatProviderError` `TimeoutException` branch). The agent can retry/degrade; it never hangs.

## Env override precedence (one resolution order, documented)

`FA_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (positive integer seconds) folds into the EXISTING `providerTimeoutsOverride` mechanism at boot (`applyProviderTimeoutEnvOverride` in `cli_config.dart`, called from `bin/fah.dart`) — it sets the new `ProviderTimeoutsOverride.fetchRead` field. Resolution order: **env wins over the `providerTimeouts:` yaml section, both win over the defaults** (a CI runner tightens the bound without editing `~/.fah/config.yaml`; same env-wins pattern as `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Per-field: the yaml section keeps governing `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the env var governs only the non-streaming fetch read bound. Invalid values fail loud with a `ConfigException` naming the env var.

Defaults: read 120s, connect 30s — the connect leg is capped by the read budget, so one knob tightens both.

Scope notes:
- the env override is per-boot: the resilience settings flow re-publishes `providerTimeoutsOverride` from the yaml section on write, which drops an env-set `fetchRead` until restart (documented behavior, not worth extra state).
- no new yaml key (`fetchReadTimeoutMs`) — env-only by design; add a yaml key when file-level control is actually needed.

## Ask-item 3 (watchdog resume poisoning) — follow-up, not implemented

No poisoned-session machinery exists in-repo; marking sessions after a provider-hang death needs death-cause tracking from the external FA-TRACE-STALE-WATCHDOG through session state and a skip rule in `--continue` — not a small clean addition. With items 1+2 the scenario dissolves in practice: the resume can no longer re-enter an unbounded call — the same call now errors within ≤150s and the resumed turn makes visible progress.

## Verification

TDD: red first (hanging `MockClient` on each fixed path), then green:
- new tests: `sendProviderFetch` connect/read legs + defaults + env cap; aiin hanging endpoint; ChatGPT OAuth hanging token endpoint; codex hanging `/responses` send → `ErrorEvent` names endpoint + timeout; env fold (valid/blank/invalid).
- targeted suites all green: provider_common, aiin_auth, chatgpt_oauth, chatgpt_codex, cli_config (198) + codemie_sso, copilot_device_flow, remote_catalog, models_for_endpoint, dial, openrouter_oauth, sse_idle_watchdog, shared_http_client, codex_transport, settings_flow_resilience (155). Streaming-path watchdog tests (sse_idle_watchdog, existing codex/copilot suites) pass untouched.
- `dart analyze` scoped to changed surfaces: no issues.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

8-12. Tests.

Key review areas:

1. **Resource leak in `sendProviderFetch`**: when `Response.fromStream` times out, the underlying `StreamedResponse` is abandoned but its stream subscription is not cancelled. Same on connect timeout — the `client.send(request)` future is abandoned. The docstring acknowledges: "The underlying socket is not force-closed on timeout (same ceiling as the streaming connect watchdog)". For the read leg, when `http.Response.fromStream(streamed)` times out, the streamed response's stream keeps buffering. Actually with package:http, if the response stream is not fully read/closed, the connection remains open. Over time this could leak sockets. The doc acknowledges it. It matches existing patterns presumably (`_sendWatched` similar). Let me check `_sendWatched` in provider_common.dart.

2. **`bin/fah.dart` try/catch** — `applyProviderTimeoutEnvOverride` throws `ConfigException` for invalid values → `_fail`. Good.

3. **In `aiin_auth.dart`**: previously `(client ?? http.Client()).send(request)` — note that when `client == null`, a NEW `http.Client()` was created and... was it closed? {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: bare TimeoutException rendering breaks failover/queue classification for every watchdog timeout**

The new branch in `formatProviderError` renders `TimeoutException` bare (no `"TimeoutException: "` prefix). But the rendered `errorMessage` is the *contract* the model-roles failover chain and the providers-queue runtime classify on:

- `lib/src/model_roles/fallback_stream.dart` `_transportPatterns` matches `timeout ?exception` / `request (attempt )?timed? ?out` — its own doc comment says watchdog timeouts are "always retryable", and `test/model_roles/fallback_stream_test.dart:1295` pins `'TimeoutException after 0:03:00.000000: Future not completed'` as transient (that shape came from `TimeoutException.toString()`, which the new branch no longer renders).
- `lib/src/model_roles/providers_queue_runtime.dart` `_timeoutPatterns` matches `timeout ?exception` the same way.

Verified empirically against `isTransientTransportError` — all of these now classify **false** (pre-PR they were `true` via the `TimeoutException` word in `toString()`):

| Message (as rendered post-PR) | transient? |
|---|---|
| `Future timed out after 3:00` (`_sendWatched` connect watchdog, all streaming adapters) | ❌ was ✅ |
| `no events from the endpoint for 300s (stream idle timeout)` (SSE idle watchdog, all adapters) | ❌ was ✅ |
| `provider fetch (…): no response headers within 30s (connect watchdog)` | ❌ |
| `provider fetch (…): response did not complete within 120s (read watchdog…)` | ❌ |
| `chatgpt-codex … timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)` | ❌ |

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the comment claims "the SSE consumption below keeps its own pacing" — it doesn't; codex mid-stream stalls still hang forever**

`run()` consumes the body with a raw loop:

```dart
await for (final line
    in response.stream
        .transform(utf8.decoder)
        .transform(const LineSplitter())) { ... }
```

There is no idle watchdog anywhere on this path — the shared `createSseIterator` / `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator` (provider_common.dart) is what gives the *other* adapters their `providerStreamIdleTimeout` pacing, and codex bypasses it (`grep -n "sseIdle\|idleWatchdog\|streamIdle" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` → nothing; `test/providers/sse_idle_watchdog_test.dart` doesn't cover codex). `grep -n "timeout(" lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex.dart` shows only this new send timeout.

So after headers arrive (the leg this PR bounds), an endpoint that stalls mid-SSE still hangs the turn indefinitely — `cancelToken.throwIfCancelled()` only helps when a token exists. That is precisely the "resume re-entered the same hang" scenario the PR says "dissolves in practice" once items 1+2 land: for codex it does not.

Suggestion: route the codex consumption through `createSseIterator(response, cancelToken)` like the other adapters (gives the idle watchdog + the issue-#921 safe abandonment for free), or at minimum correct this comment so the audit table's "streaming adapters … + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact" claim is true for codex.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the read-leg timeout abandons the response body without cancelling/draining it**

On read timeout, `http.Response.fromStream(streamed).timeout(read, …)` leaves the body subscription alive and nobody drains or cancels it:

- The socket can never return to the keep-alive pool (undrained response), and a server that keeps trickling bytes into the abandoned stream buffers them until the socket dies.
- On the **shared** client this poisons a pooled connection: `chatgpt_codex.dart:341` passes the shared keep-alive client into `refreshChatGptCredentials` → `_tokenRequest` → `sendProviderFetch`, and `runProviderStream` never closes it (`ownsClient: false`). This is the same abandonment class issue #921 solved for the SSE path (`_IdleWatchdogSseIterator`'s `onAbandon` + owned error sink).

The docstring's ceiling note covers the *connect* leg (no headers yet — nothing to drain). For the read leg a cheap improvement: race `fromStream` against a timer and on timeout `unawaited(streamed.stream.drain<void>().timeout(...))` (or listen-and-cancel), so the connection closes/reuses cleanly.

Related nit: `aiin_auth.dart:415` creates `http.Client()` when `client == null` and never closes it — `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` right next door shows the `ownsClient` + `finally { httpClient.close() }` pattern; adopting it bounds the leak on this path too.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1108
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1108
- **Title**: fix(#1036): bound provider HTTP calls with client-side timeouts
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1036` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +406
- **Deletions**: -26
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T11:46:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T12:18:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1036

## What hung, what is bounded now

Audited every provider HTTP call in `lib/src/providers/` (the shared `sharedProviderHttpClient` plus every direct `http.Client` use):

| Path | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `aiin_auth._postOrGet` (OAuth providers list, code exchange, API-key registration) | **no timeout at all** — the issue's hang | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s) |
| `chatgpt_codex._request` (`/responses` send) | **no watchdog** — the only unbounded send in the streaming adapters | `.timeout(effectiveProviderConnectTimeout)` with a message naming the endpoint (same bound as `_sendWatched`) |
| `chatgpt_oauth._tokenRequest` (exchange + refresh) | hard-coded 30s, not configurable | `sendProviderFetch` (connect 30s / read 120s, configurable) |
| models lists (`models_for_endpoint`, 4 dialects) | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate fail-fast prefetch budget |
| remote catalog | 10s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| codemie sso (3 calls) / openrouter oauth | 30s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| dial models info | 15s hard | unchanged — deliberate |
| copilot device flow + token exchange | `effectiveProviderConnectTimeout` | unchanged — already configurable via yaml |
| streaming adapters (anthropic, google, dial, openai, copilot, llm relay) | `sendProviderRequest`/`_sendWatched` + SSE idle watchdog | unchanged and intact (all existing watchdog tests pass) |

On timeout every fixed path fails with a `TimeoutException` whose message names the endpoint class and the leg (connect vs read) — aiin wraps into `AiinAuthException`, ChatGPT OAuth into `ConfigException`, codex surfaces via the errors-as-events `ErrorEvent` (message rendered bare by the new `formatProviderError` `TimeoutException` branch). The agent can retry/degrade; it never hangs.

## Env override precedence (one resolution order, documented)

`FA_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (positive integer seconds) folds into the EXISTING `providerTimeoutsOverride` mechanism at boot (`applyProviderTimeoutEnvOverride` in `cli_config.dart`, called from `bin/fah.dart`) — it sets the new `ProviderTimeoutsOverride.fetchRead` field. Resolution order: **env wins over the `providerTimeouts:` yaml section, both win over the defaults** (a CI runner tightens the bound without editing `~/.fah/config.yaml`; same env-wins pattern as `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`). Per-field: the yaml section keeps governing `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the env var governs only the non-streaming fetch read bound. Invalid values fail loud with a `ConfigException` naming the env var.

Defaults: read 120s, connect 30s — the connect leg is capped by the read budget, so one knob tightens both.

Scope notes:
- the env override is per-boot: the resilience settings flow re-publishes `providerTimeoutsOverride` from the yaml section on write, which drops an env-set `fetchRead` until restart (documented behavior, not worth extra state).
- no new yaml key (`fetchReadTimeoutMs`) — env-only by design; add a yaml key when file-level control is actually needed.

## Ask-item 3 (watchdog resume poisoning) — follow-up, not implemented

No poisoned-session machinery exists in-repo; marking sessions after a provider-hang death needs death-cause tracking from the external FA-TRACE-STALE-WATCHDOG through session state and a skip rule in `--continue` — not a small clean addition. With items 1+2 the scenario dissolves in practice: the resume can no longer re-enter an unbounded call — the same call now errors within ≤150s and the resumed turn makes visible progress.

## Verification

TDD: red first (hanging `MockClient` on each fixed path), then green:
- new tests: `sendProviderFetch` connect/read legs + defaults + env cap; aiin hanging endpoint; ChatGPT OAuth hanging token endpoint; codex hanging `/responses` send → `ErrorEvent` names endpoint + timeout; env fold (valid/blank/invalid).
- targeted suites all green: provider_common, aiin_auth, chatgpt_oauth, chatgpt_codex, cli_config (198) + codemie_sso, copilot_device_flow, remote_catalog, models_for_endpoint, dial, openrouter_oauth, sse_idle_watchdog, shared_http_client, codex_transport, settings_flow_resilience (155). Streaming-path watchdog tests (sse_idle_watchdog, existing codex/copilot suites) pass untouched.
- `dart analyze` scoped to changed surfaces: no issues.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
